title: Erdős Problem #481: Affine Sequence Iteration and Eventual Repetition
description: For affine maps T with Σ(1/aᵢ) > 1, iterating from A₁=(1) must eventually produce repeated elements. Proved by Klarner (1982) using free semigroup theory.

overview.historicalContext: This problem appears in Erdős and Graham's book *Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory* (1980, p.96). They remarked that 'it is surprising that [this problem] offers difficulty,' noting the innocent appearance of the iteration process. Klarner provided the first proof in 1982 by connecting the problem to free semigroups of affine maps: the density condition Σ(1/aᵢ) > 1 precisely characterizes when the affine semigroup generated by {x ↦ aᵢx + bᵢ} is **non-free** — non-freeness implies that some composition of maps coincides, manifesting as a collision in the iteration. The threshold Σ(1/aᵢ) = 1 is exactly the Bernoulli condition for the existence of infinite collision-free orbits. Alweiss (2021) showed that an extra minimum-value condition Erdős and Graham had included was in fact redundant, simplifying the statement. Kolpakov and Talambutsa (2022) generalized these results to affine maps on the real line, connecting the problem to the theory of self-similar fractals and Hausdorff dimension.
overview.problemStatement: Let a₁,...,aᵣ,b₁,...,bᵣ ∈ ℕ such that Σᵢ(1/aᵢ) > 1. For a sequence A = (x₁,...,xₙ), define T(A) = (aᵢxⱼ + bᵢ) for all i,j. Prove that if A₁ = (1) and Aₖ₊₁ = T(Aₖ), then some Aₖ must have repeated elements.
overview.text: For affine maps T with Σ(1/aᵢ) > 1, iterating from A₁=(1) must eventually produce repeated elements. Proved by Klarner (1982) using free semigroup theory.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization defines affine transformations, the density condition Σ(1/aᵢ) > 1, and the iteration process. The key result (Klarner 1982) is axiomatized: the density condition forces collisions because it corresponds to the affine semigroup being non-free. The density intuition is that intervals of length N/aᵢ covering [0,N] have total length exceeding N, so pigeonhole forces overlaps.
keyInsights: The density condition Σ(1/aᵢ) > 1 is crucial and tight
Relates to free semigroups: non-free ⟹ relations ⟹ collisions
Value range grows, but slower than length when density > 1
Boundary case: Σ(1/aᵢ) = 1 is the exact threshold
Original extra condition on minimum was redundant (Alweiss)

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #481 is SOLVED. The conjecture that Σ(1/aᵢ) > 1 forces eventual repetition in affine sequence iteration is TRUE (Klarner 1982). The proof connects to algebraic semigroup theory: the density condition characterizes when the affine semigroup is non-free, and non-freeness implies relations that manifest as collisions.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: This result bridges number theory and algebra.

The density condition Σ(1/aᵢ) > 1 appears in various contexts related to covering and self-affine structures. The semigroup perspective has been extended by Kolpakov-Talambutsa (2022) to more general affine maps.
